diagnostic_evidence.quote: the product $v_0 v_1 v_2^2 \approx \tau^{\frac{3}{2}} \e^{-\tau (|x-x_0|^2 + (t-t_0)^2)}$ near the point $(x_0, t_0)$

issues.failure_explanation: With H(l)=phi_h(l) tau^{1/2} e^{-tau l^2/2}, the actual product is v_0 v_1 v_2^2 = phi_h^3 tau^{3/2} exp(-(tau/2)[(s-y)^2+(s+y)^2+(s-z)^2]) with s=t-t_0, y=theta.(x-x_0), z=theta^perp.(x-x_0). The exponent is -tau*Phi with Phi = (3/2)s^2 + y^2 + (1/2)z^2 - s z, which is not s^2+y^2+z^2 = (t-t_0)^2+|x-x_0|^2. Hence the claimed isotropic Gaussian concentration is false and Lemma lemma:approx identity q does not apply as invoked. In the orthonormal coordinates (s,y,z) the quadratic form Phi has matrix with determinant 1/2, so tau^{3/2} \int q e^{-tau Phi} -> sqrt(2) pi^{3/2} q(x_0,t_0), and via the identity (2.6) (3! int q v_0 v_1 v_2^2 = boundary integral) the right-hand side of (2.16) converges to 3! sqrt(2) pi^{3/2} q(x_0,t_0), not to 3! pi^{3/2} q(x_0,t_0). The formula's normalization is wrong by a factor sqrt(2).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false isotropic product claim with the correct anisotropic Gaussian and change the constant in (2.16) from 3! pi^{3/2} to 3! sqrt(2) pi^{3/2}, justified by the routine positive-definite-Gaussian variant of Lemma lemma:approx identity q (or choose different waves and re-derive the constant).
issues.overall_effect: The pointwise reconstruction identity (2.16) and its numerical implementation (used for the comparison reconstructions in Section 4) return sqrt(2) q(x_0,t_0) instead of q(x_0,t_0); pointwise amplitudes are quantitatively wrong by a constant factor. The Radon-based main results and the stability theory are unaffected.
issues.title: Pointwise reconstruction formula (2.16) is off by a factor of sqrt(2) (false isotropic-Gaussian product claim)
issues.why_classification: The defect is a wrong constant in a secondary, comparison-only formula; the repair is a short, local, routine correction (a 3x3 Gaussian determinant computation) that preserves the pointwise reconstruction claim and every other substantive result, with no new lemma, construction, or global argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We define the admissible reconstruction domain by setting $T>4r$, $t_1>2r$, $t_2<T-2r$, and defining
For the numerical solution of the forward problem we use the parameters $N_{x_1} = N_{x_2} = 80$ and $N_t = 1500$ in the space domain $\Omega = [-0.5, 0.5]^2$ and time domain $[0, T] = [0, 3]$.
$P$ corresponds to the interval $[-0.4, 0.4]$ divided into $63$ equally spaced distances from the origin

issues.failure_explanation: The reconstruction (2.11) is justified only for tuples in W_Radon, i.e. times t_0 in [t_1,t_2] with t_1>2r and t_2<T-2r. For Omega=[-0.5,0.5]^2 the smallest enclosing ball has r=sqrt(2)/2~0.7071, so with T=3 admissible times lie in (1.414,1.586); but the algorithm reconstructs at t_0=T/2+eta_0 in [1.1,1.9] for eta_0 in P=[-0.4,0.4], so every row with |eta_0| larger than about 0.086 lies outside the paper's admissible regime. Admissibility is precisely what guarantees the plane wave H_2(x,t)=H(-x.theta_0 - t + eta_0 + t_0) vanishes (with its t-derivative) inside Omega at t=T, so that the auxiliary solution v_0 of (2.5) equals this plane wave and the integration-by-parts identity (2.6) holds with no final-time terms. For eta_0 near +0.4, l(x,T) = -x.theta_0 - 1.5 + 2 eta_0 vanishes at x.theta_0 = 2 eta_0 - 1.5 in (-r,r) (e.g. eta_0=0.4 gives x.theta_0=-0.7, and 0.7<r=0.7071): the wave peak is inside Omega at t=T, so v_0 differs from H_2 and unknown final-time terms involving w(T), partial_t w(T) enter (2.6); the measured boundary integral is then not the claimed line integral. Any cutoff width h compatible with tau=700 (Gaussian width ~0.038) gives failure for eta_0 > (0.7929-h)/2. Hence the stated guarantee of reconstructing the entire sinogram column over P is unsupported for most distances and false at the extreme ones.

failure_location.quote: More specifically, for each $\eta_0 \in P$, we set the auxiliary function $v_0$ corresponding to $(\frac{T}{2} + \eta_0, \theta_0, \eta_0)$ as in Section \ref{sec: choosing boundary for radon}. With these choices, we can reconstruct $\radonR(q)^{\text{rec}}(\frac{T}{2} + \eta_0, \theta_0, \eta_0) = \radonR(q)^{\text{rec}}(\theta_0, \eta_0)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the reconstruction to tuples satisfying the support/admissibility conditions, e.g. increase the final time to T > 2r + 2h + 4 sup|eta_0| (about T >= 3.3 for P=[-0.4,0.4] with realistic h) or shrink P to eta_0 < (T/2 - r - h)/2 (about eta_0 <= 0.35 for h=0.1), and recompute the numerical examples; equivalently, verify the zero-final-time support condition row by row before claiming each sinogram value.
issues.overall_effect: The algorithm's claimed output R(q)^rec(theta_0, eta_0) for all eta_0 in P=[-0.4,0.4] (and the matching Figure 1 caption claim) is not covered by the paper's theory and is mathematically incorrect as described for rows near eta_0=0.4; the affected sinogram rows, and consequently the outer regions of the filtered-backprojection reconstructions in the examples, are unreliable. The theoretical results of Section 2, stated only on the admissible set, are unaffected.
issues.title: Sinogram algorithm reconstructs over distances whose parameter tuples violate the paper's admissibility/support conditions; auxiliary wave fails the zero final condition near eta_0 = 0.4
issues.why_classification: The Section 2 theory survives unchanged, but the described and implemented procedure operates outside its own validity hypotheses over part of its advertised output range and fails at the extremes; every correct resolution alters the numerical protocol (larger T or reduced P) and requires regenerating the computational results -- a contained reoptimization/limited weakening leaving a recognizably comparable result, with no new proof architecture.
